title: ERL2 adapter platform: protocol, sandbox, capability, credential, mutation and certification contracts
$comment: Design v2 §11.2/§11.3/§21, implementation plan §11. Every object is closed. Nothing here may carry a plaintext secret, a truth or judge reference, a selection handle, or a validity verdict: the adapter plane has none of those authorities.

AdapterOperationId.$comment: Closed operation set, one per SubjectAdapterV1 method (design v2 §11.2). An operation outside this set is refused with ADAPTER_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED.

AdapterCapabilityId.$comment: Closed capability enum. There is no arbitrary-shell capability at all. The privileged members exist so that a request for one is a typed refusal rather than an unrecognised string; ERL2-OQ-001 keeps every one of them ungrantable.

SandboxControlId.$comment: Isolation controls the host may claim. Each is reported as enforced or unsupported_on_this_host with a reason; an unsupported control is never reported as enforced (design v2 §21 residual-risk rule). The distinction matters: a control the host *adjudicates* (it decides and receipts every declared attempt) is not the same as a control the kernel *prevents*, and they are separate members here so a report cannot conflate them.

AdapterProtocolNegotiationV1.$comment: The one handshake. The host offers exactly one protocol version and refuses any adapter that answers with another (ADAPTER_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH).

AdapterResponseEnvelopeV1.$comment: What an adapter returns for one operation. `unsupported` is a first-class retained outcome, never an omission (ERL2-FR-005). There is no validity, threshold, score or truth field.

owner.$comment: An adapter may attribute a failure to itself or to the subject it wraps. It can never attribute one to the Lab, the evaluator or a dependency; only core owns those domains.

allOf.$comment: A supported outcome carries a result and no error; a failed or unsupported outcome carries an error.
Only an unsupported outcome may list unsupported inputs.

AdapterCapabilityGrantV1.$comment: The capability broker's decision. Under ERL2-OQ-001 every privileged capability is denied, and the denial is recorded rather than emulated (ERL2-SEC-003, ERL2-AC-017).

MutationIntentV1.$comment: Declared before the external mutation happens. Intent -> receipt -> event -> snapshot is the only permitted order (design v2 §6.3/§20).

allOf.$comment: A failed mutation must state why.

CompensationReceiptV1.$comment: Every mutation receipt names a compensation identity, and the compensation receipt must name the same mutation and the same target (ERL2-OPS-001).

CredentialHandleRequestV1.$comment: A credential is requested as a scoped handle. Every property here is an identifier, a hash, an enum or a bounded integer: the contract has no field a plaintext secret could occupy (ERL2-SEC-001).

CredentialHandleGrantV1.$comment: Requested, granted and denied scopes are recorded separately so an over-broad request is visible even when the broker narrowed it (ERL2-AC-011).

CredentialUseReceiptV1.$comment: Each use is bound to run, adapter, operation and target. Reuse outside scope, after expiry, beyond max uses, or from another run is denied and receipted as denied.

EgressAllowlistPolicyV1.$comment: Deny by default. Loopback, link-local, metadata services and proxy bypass are denied unless the policy names them explicitly, and there is no wildcard host form.

allow_loopback_hosts.$comment: Explicitly granted loopback hosts only; an empty array is the default and denies loopback entirely.

SandboxInvocationManifestV1.$comment: Exactly what the host will run and exactly what it will expose. `enforced_controls` reports each isolation control as enforced or unsupported_on_this_host; a control the host cannot actually apply is never listed as enforced (design v2 §21).

sandbox_profile.$comment: The profile this invocation ran under. Absent means `local-process`, which is what every manifest frozen before the container-backed launcher existed described; the `enforced_controls` list is the discriminator either way.

isolation_substrate_lock_hash.$comment: Core hash of the `IsolationSubstrateLockV1` whose observed enforcement evidence licenses this invocation's control report. Required when `sandbox_profile` is `container`: a container manifest that named no substrate would claim kernel-prevented controls with nothing behind them.

environment_variable_names.$comment: Allowlisted names only. Values are never recorded, so this contract cannot become a secret channel.

allOf.$comment: A container-profile manifest must name the substrate lock whose observed evidence licenses its control report; there is no representable container invocation that claims kernel-prevented controls without one.

container_termination.$comment: What the runtime was *observed* to report about the container after the invocation ended. Present only for the container profile. `process_tree_terminated` above is the verdict; this is the measurement it was derived from, so an offline reader can disagree with the verdict. Identity is the full container id read at create time — never a bare pid, which the NC-PROCTREE negative control caught being reused.

namespace_processes_at_termination.$comment: Processes the runtime listed inside the container's pid namespace at the moment termination was ordered. Zero for a container that had already exited.

residue_after_removal.$comment: True when the runtime still knows the container id after removal was ordered; a residue failure, not a cleanup detail.

deadline_span_ms.$comment: Real elapsed milliseconds from arming the deadline to observing the container not running. The measurement the ADR-ERL2-017 §Evidence defect would have failed on: a deadline that took the container's full run to take effect bounded nothing.

SubjectDiagnosticsManifestV1.$comment: Bounded, scanned and redacted before retention (ERL2-SEC-004). A positive canary count is a Lab integrity failure, never a subject-quality result.

AdapterFailureReportV1.$comment: A typed adapter/Lab ownership record. `subject_attribution_proven` is const false: a broken or malicious adapter can never be recorded as a subject defect (ERL2-OPS-003, ERL2-AC-003).

SubjectAdapterCertificationReceiptV1.$comment: ADAPTER-CERT-V1. `certifier_is_adapter_owner` is const false: an adapter cannot self-certify (design v2 §11.3). Certification permits an adapter version/digest; it never certifies subject quality.

allOf.$comment: A refused verdict must name at least one refusal code; a certified one names none.
